text:
alice_support: Hey team — Customer ACME (org_id: org-482) reports p95/p99 spikes starting ~2026-03-14T15:02Z. They see a bunch of 10s+ responses and errors. They provided example request ids: r-4ab2, r-4ab5, r-4ac0. Can eng take a look? :wave:

monitor-bot: ALERT: High request queue length on inference-workers-prod (queue_depth > 110) at 2026-03-14T15:04Z. p99 latency for /v1/generate = 12.8s (baseline 0.45s).

ben_oncall: Acknowledging. I pulled metrics — cluster-wide avg concurrency per worker spiked from 8 -> 38 in that window. Admission controller logs show repeated "queue_full" decisions.

priya_runtime: Thanks. Can you paste the admission-controller logs? I'm wondering if batching/kv cache thrash is implicated.

ben_oncall: Paste excerpt: ```
2026-03-14T15:03:12Z admission: tenant=org-482 decision=enqueue queue_len=95 max_concurrency=20
2026-03-14T15:03:13Z admission: tenant=org-482 decision=reject reason=queue_full
2026-03-14T15:03:14Z worker: id=iw-47 cpu=92% mem=78% inflight=46
2026-03-14T15:03:15Z admission: tenant=org-482 decision=enqueue queue_len=101
```

marco_sre: Noticing similar pattern in other tenants but ACME hit a steady burst for ~6m. Any deploys around that time?

deploy-bot: Deploy started by ci:infra at 2026-03-14T14:58Z -> infra/admission-controller:v2.4.6 -> status: success 2026-03-14T15:01:30Z.

priya_runtime: Interesting — admission-controller bumped to v2.4.6 right before the spike. New release changed per-tenant concurrency accounting to be more strict (PR notes). Could be miscalibrated thresholds.

alice_support: Customer reports it started "suddenly" after 15:00 UTC — lines up with that deploy. They're asking for mitigation asap.

ben_oncall: For mitigation I'm going to temporarily increase tenant max_concurrency for org-482 from 20 -> 60 and scale up worker pool by +4 GPU pods. Doing now.

priya_runtime: Small warning: if we raise tenant limit we might push other tenants into queue. But ok as short-term. I'm reverting a config flag on admission-controller to the previous behavior in a canary. Rolling back on canary nodes first.

marco_sre: Thumbs on scaling: autoscaler allowed +4 nodes; new workers registered at 15:06Z. Queue depth back to ~20 by 15:08Z, p99 dropped to 0.7s.

alice_support: Customer confirmation: "latency back to normal around 15:09, huge relief". They still saw a few 5s responses during mitigation window.

priya_runtime: Repro steps collected: load test script (run from prod-sim): ```bash
for i in {1..500}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"model":"llamax-13b","input":"short prompt"}' &
done
wait
``` We observed same queue_full decisions when concurrency distribution hit the new strict accounting threshold.

ben_oncall: Short-term postmortem notes: 1) Rollback admission-controller config on all nodes (completed 15:12Z). 2) Increase per-tenant soft limit temporarily for ACME. 3) Opened support ticket with ACME and offered credits.

priya_runtime: Root cause hypothesis: v2.4.6 changed "effective_concurrency" calc to include queued requests *per-tenant* rather than just inflight. Under bursty traffic this double-counted requests and under-estimated available slots -> aggressive rejects and queue buildup. Repro in staging with synthetic burst confirms similar behavior.

marco_sre: Evidence: timeline of admission decisions spikes + deploy event + reproduction in staging. Also saw worker-side logs indicating heavy KV-cache misses at burst start -> extra cpu/time per request. That amplifies impact.

alice_support: Customer question: will this recur or is it fixed?

priya_runtime: We've pushed a hotfix to admission-controller to restore previous counting logic and added a feature-flag guard. Hotfix PR: gh/infra/admission#813 (merged 15:20Z). Rolling restart running now. Plan: monitor for 30m.

deploy-bot: Rolling restart of infra/admission-controller triggered (batch=25% nodes) at 15:22Z.

monitor-bot: UPDATE: queue_depth reduced to <10 across cluster at 15:27Z. p99 back to 0.6s. No error spikes observed after patches.

jules_custsuccess: Follow-up with ACME sent: summary, RCA draft, compensation offer, ask to share any additional logs. They appreciated fast response.

ben_oncall: Action items: - eng-runtime: add unit test for concurrency calc edge cases (priya) - eng-sre: add dashboard alert on "deploy->queue_depth correlation" (marco) - support: prepare customer-facing RCA (alice/jules) - infra: consider rolling back v2.4.6 changes until tested on multi-tenant bursts.

priya_runtime: Adding to backlog: make admission-controller config opt-in per-tenant and add canary traffic simulation before global rollout.

alice_support: Thanks everyone. I'll update the ticket and close once customer acknowledges RCA. :white_check_mark:

ben_oncall: Closing note: short-term mitigations prevented major outage. Will follow up on long-term fixes in next sprint.

alice_support: (closing) ACME acknowledged RCA and accepted credits. Marking as resolved. :tada:
